Stated Claim / Post Context:
Influencer slammed for posing amid the rubble and destruction after Panama's devastating earthquake

Popular social media star Gracie Bon, who has nearly 12 million followers on Instagram, came under fierce fire after she shared a series of photos of herself standing among the destroyed buildings.

Actual Article Body:
By LILLIAN GISSEN, US DEPUTY LIFESTYLE EDITOR

Updated:  06:10 AEDT, 14 October 2026

An influencer has been furiously slammed online after she posed amid the rubble and destruction in Panama following the devastating earthquake last week.

Popular social media star Gracie Bon, who has nearly 12 million followers on Instagram, came under fierce fire after she shared a series of photos of herself standing among destroyed buildings on Sunday.

One image showed her standing on top of wreckage with her hands up in the air, while another saw her kneeling in front of a broken house as she looked away from the camera.

The social media star donned a pair of blue jeans and a white, button-down crop top that accentuated her curves.

'The reality of my country after the earthquake,' she captioned the post.

'We have to remember that the material is recovered, but life is priceless. Live the present, be grateful for what we have and extend help to those who need it today.'

Bon's post sparked immense backlash, as many rushed to the comment section to bash her for doing a 'photo shoot' amongst the debris and accused her of using the tragedy for content.

'I would never take a picture in the middle of a tragedy, people and their stuff,' wrote one user. 'Strength to those going through a difficult time right now.'

Popular social media star Gracie Bon has come under fierce fire after she shared a series of photos of herself posing amid the rubble and destruction in Panama following the devastating earthquake last week

Bon's post sparked immense backlash, as many rushed to the comment section to bash her for doing a 'photo shoot' amongst the debris and accused her of using the tragedy for content, however, she claimed it was posted to try to help get donations for victims

'Unbelievable... Just for looking for likes,' slammed another.

'Posing with someone else's misfortune must be a joke,' someone else added.

'"How do I make this about me?" What a need to go out posing in the middle of a disaster,' read a fourth comment.

A fifth said: 'I can't believe she actually asked someone to take pictures of her in front of someone's destroyed house.'

'Did you seriously hire a photographer to go to the affected area to take some photos?' asked a different user.

'There is a huge difference between documenting a tragedy to raise awareness and using the location where it occurred as a backdrop for a photograph,' pointed out another outraged fan.

The massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit Panama southwest of Pitaloza Arriba, a village of just over 100 residents in Herrera province, on Friday.

Reports of collapsed buildings, split roads and caved-in roofs emerged after the quake, with authorities saying damage was concentrated in central Panama.

Bon has nearly 12 million followers on Instagram

No deaths have been reported, but at least 27 people were injured and nearly 900 homes have been damaged, according to Reuters.

Amid the backlash, Bon defended herself in a comment, explaining that she posted the photos to try to show the 'reality of her country' after the earthquake because 'many news [sites] don't show it.'

'CONTEXT: These photos are the reality of the country. Many news [sites] don't show it, many media says "Panama is fine" and they don't show the reality of the affected areas, the people who lost their homes,' she wrote.

She said she wanted to encourage her followers to 'make donations' and knew that if she 'appeared in the photos' they would have a 'better reach.'

'I decided to appear in my photos because I want people to make donations and if I appear in my photos they have a better reach on MY NETWORKS than if I put the images alone,' she continued.

'I'm not in a photoshoot or posing, I'm telling y'all "Look, this is how Panama really is."'

'But you have a damaged heart that prefers to insult and not help the cause,' she added to her haters.

The massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake hit Panama southwest of Pitaloza Arriba, a village of just over 100 residents in Herrera province, on Friday

'If I hadn't been in the picture, would it be okay? The [more important] question is: What is everyone doing to contribute?'

Earlier that day, Bon shared a video of herself stocking up on supplies like cases of bottled water and bags of rice to donate to victims.

She was then seen traveling to the area and handing them out to families.

'Panama needs us. While some today are fortunate enough to be safe in our homes, there are families who have lost almost everything and do not know where they will sleep tonight,' she captioned it.

'Today I bring a grain of [rice], what to us is little, to someone else it may mean so much.'

She also included addresses of places where people can drop off 'water, non-perishable food, hygiene products, diapers and basic necessities' to donate.

'If you can't donate, sharing is also a way to help,' she added.

Bon posted a video addressing the backlash on Monday, insisting that she hadn't made any money from the post.

'Instead of talking about [the families who lost their homes], they are talking about a picture of me,' she said.

'Many are only behind the keyboard criticizing and they do not [answer] the question, "What have you done so far to help Panama?"

'Tomorrow you will forget about my photo, but that family will remain without a home.'

'There are people who get more outraged by a photo than by seeing families lose everything. Sometimes the problem is not what we do, but the eyes with which you decide to see it,' she added in the caption. 'Let's help Panama.'
